source_document.body:
Becton Dickinson (BD) plans to invest $19 billion in the United States over several years under an agreement with the federal government that ties expanded domestic manufacturing to relief from future tariffs . The medical device maker will direct $3 billion of that total toward manufacturing expansion , with the rest going toward U.S. operations and supply chain investments.
What’s Related
The company announced the agreement on Oct. 6. It plans to add approximately 5 billion essential medical consumables to its annual U.S. production and raise the share of those products it supplies domestically to roughly 80%.
BD also plans to manufacture all of its needles used in America domestically, using American-made steel. The announcement did not provide a completion date, a plant-by-plant spending breakdown, or a total number of new jobs .
Reuters reported that the agreement is the first between a major U.S. medical device company and the government linking domestic manufacturing commitments to tariff relief. President Donald Trump said more than $1 billion would go to Nebraska.
Tariff relief comes with conditions
Under BD’s agreement, relief would apply to covered products and manufacturing inputs under future Section 232 tariff actions. It depends on the final rules and BD reaching agreed milestones.
The company has not calculated the financial impact because tariff rates, covered products, and effective dates remain unsettled. BD expects to provide more information once the tariffs are finalized.
That leaves two important details unresolved: how much the company could save and which products and inputs would qualify. The announcement also does not identify the milestones BD must meet to receive relief.
Nebraska expansion already underway
The commitment follows BD’s January announcement of a $110 million investment in Columbus, Nebraska, expected to create approximately 120 jobs. The project will bring production of its Neopak glass prefillable syringes to the site for use with biologic and GLP-1 drugs.
BD allocated $100 million to syringe production and related line upgrades, plus $10 million to cannula manufacturing. In January, it said supply from the new syringe production would begin in mid-2026; the October announcement did not provide an updated status.
The Columbus work followed a separate investment of more than $35 million to expand prefilled flush syringe manufacturing and add approximately 50 jobs. The site has operated for more than 75 years and includes cannula design and production.
